subject.title: [Feature]: Make detached longwork final delivery ownership explicit

question: Which substrate should own durable final-summary delivery for detached or migrated long-running subagent work: native subagent metadata, a broader pending-final/outbox delivery obligation, or a narrower channel-specific route contract?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent contract affects runtime API shape, session state, hook metadata, and message-delivery guarantees across sibling workflows, so automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Use a broader delivery-obligation substrate
options.body: Define final-summary ownership in the durable pending-final/outbox path and have native subagents, background work, and channel bridges share that contract.

options.title: Keep it native-subagent scoped
options.body: Add explicit native completion owner modes only for sessions_spawn/subagents and leave ACP/background/channel-specific delivery semantics to separate issues.

options.title: Defer to channel-specific repairs
options.body: Avoid a generic owner contract for now and repair only the proven Discord or Slack route-loss cases as they are reproduced.

recommendation.title: Use a broader delivery-obligation substrate
recommendation.body: Define final-summary ownership in the durable pending-final/outbox path and have native subagents, background work, and channel bridges share that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The current requester/completion session-key split in this area comes from Jerry-Xin's merged #80242 work, making them the strongest code-history owner for deciding whether to extend or replace that contract.
